newsitem.title: CANADA: MOTOR RACING-HOME HOPE VILLENEUVE OUTSHONE BY SCHUMACHER.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-HOME HOPE VILLENEUVE OUTSHONE BY SCHUMACHER.

text.p: Double world champion Michael Schumacher upstaged local hero Jacques Villeneuve on Saturday when he grabbed pole position for Sunday's Canadian Grand Prix in the final seconds of a dramatic qualifying session.
Schumacher clocked a fastest time of one minute 18.095 seconds in the last 15 seconds to squeeze the championship leader out of the prime grid position.

The German's supreme effort, delivered with exquisite timing after a crash involving Austrian debutant Alexander Wurz had interrupted and delayed the session, ended the Williams team's run of 10 straight pole spot dating back to August of last year. Wurz was unhurt after hitting a wall in his Benetton.

It was Schumacher and Ferrari's first pole since the Hungarian Grand Prix last season and the 15th of his career. It also dimmed the Williams team's hopes of claiming their 100th victory since they entered Formula One with an easy triumph in Sunday's 69-lap race on the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve, named after Jacques' father.
Schumacher and Villeneuve, the outstanding rival protagonists in this year's world title chase, will share the front row of the grid.
Rubens Barrichello of Brazil was third behind them in his Stewart after a magnificent lap in the closing minutes hoisted him among the top contenders.
Villeneuve's team mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen wound up fourth quickest ahead of Briton David Coulthard in a McLaren and Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Jordan.
Schumacher's younger brother Ralf was seventh in the second Jordan and Frenchman Jean Alesi eighth in the leading Benetton.

"It is very satisfying and pleasing for me to be here on pole because I really did not expect it," admitted Schumacher. "I was able to get my quick lap in because this year I have found I can go straight out and do a fast lap and I was confident I could do it again.

"That meant I could leave it until very late in the session. Our car has improved a little with some aerodnyamic and mechanical modfications, but I did not expect them to make much major difference. On this circuit, I think they just gave us enough of an edge to help us."

Schumacher, second and three points behind Villeneuve in the drivers' championship, said he hoped to be competitive and aimed to help Ferrari hang on to their slender one point lead over Williams in the constructors' series.

Villeneuve, given a rapturous reception every time he was seen out on the track by the big crowd on the Ile Notre Dame, admitted he felt disappointed. "I am not sure this is such a good track for our car as it does not have that many fast corners which help us show up our good aerodynamics," he said. "It felt weird to me when the crowd were cheering me at the end even though I had been beaten."

Villeneuve, who was joined in the paddock by his mother Joann and sister Melanie, added: "At least there are two more races in Germany coming up this year, so I will have a good chance to get my own back."
Barrichello said he was astonished at his high place on the grid and attributed it to the use iof using very small wings on his car to maximise the speed provided by its Ford V10 engine.

Wurz's accident came five minutes from the end of the session. He lost control of his Benetton at the fast chicane on the start-finish straight and grazed the wall, spinning his car into the barrier and ripping off the front right wheel.
He said: "It was my mistake and I feel bad about it."
He was able to climb from the car and walk unaided back to the Benetton garage.
Defending world champion Damon Hill laboured to 15th place in his Arrows.
